title: Bootloader & Updates
description: Review of the bootloader, the update process over the air or in the field, failure recovery, and data migration between versions.

items.text: The bootloader is as small and simple as possible, and is never updated in the field (or safely if it is)
items.hint: A bootloader bug in the field can brick every device. Treat any bootloader update as a last resort.

items.text: The bootloader validates the application image (CRC or signature) before jumping to it
items.hint: And knows what to do when no valid image exists.

items.text: The handoff to the application resets peripherals, interrupts, and the stack pointer
items.hint: Leftover bootloader state is a classic source of rare startup bugs.

items.text: A recovery path exists for a device with no valid image (USB, UART, test pads)
items.hint: Document it for the service team.

items.text: A failed or interrupted update leaves the device running the previous image
items.hint: A/B slots or a protected recovery image. Test power loss at every stage of the update.

items.text: A new image must confirm it works before it's made permanent, or it rolls back
items.hint: Self-test after boot, then confirm. A watchdog reset before confirmation reverts.

items.text: Images are authenticated (signed) and integrity-checked before install
items.hint: Check the signature before writing to the boot slot, not after.

items.text: Updates are compatible with the hardware revision and the current version
items.hint: The image header names the hardware it's for. Refuse a mismatch.

items.text: Staged rollout and a way to stop a bad release are planned
items.hint: E.g. 1%, 10%, then everyone, with a halt if crash or rollback rates go up.

items.text: Download resumes after a dropped connection
items.hint: Large images over weak Wi-Fi rarely finish in one go.
Schedule or defer the reboot. E.g. not mid-cycle on an HVAC call.

items.text: Stored settings migrate forward across every version that can update to this one
items.hint: Test from each released version, not only the last one.

items.text: A rollback to the previous image can still read the data the new image wrote
items.hint: Or the migration happens only after the new image is confirmed.
